data.name: Anatolien
data.gender_notes: Anatolien is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Anatolia is the goddess of lands and wild animals. The name Anatolien is derived from Anatolia and means 'man of Anatolia'. In Christianity, this name could be given to a child born in Anatolia or as a symbolic representation of the land's connection to the divine. The name Anatolien carries the meaning “Man of Anatolia” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek. Parents who choose Anatolien usually hope their child will grow to embody man of anatolia and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name with strong connections to the land and its deities, representing a sense of belonging and reverence for the natural world.
data.etymology: Anatolien belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Man of Anatolia.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Anatolien total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_hebrew.name: עֲנָתוֹל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: עֲנָתוֹל היא מְעוֹרֶרֶת עוֹפַן וּמוֹסָד לְבַעֲלַת הַבּוֹקֶר. זהו שֵם הַשָּׁכַל, שֶאֵין לוֹ עַלְמָא, הַמְעוֹרֵרֶת אֶת כָּל עוֹפַן הַשָּׁכַל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּשׂוֹפְרִים 'והָלְכוּ אַחֲרֵי תְּמוּת ' .

in_greek.name: Ἀνατολίη
in_greek.meaning: Ἀνατολή, ἡμέρα, ὡς ἐν τῇ Ἀνατολίᾳ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ἀνατολίη ὀνόματα προέρχονται ἀπὸ τῆς ἑλληνιστIKῆς λέξης Ἀνατολή, ἡμέρα, ὡς ἐν τῇ Ἀνατολίᾳ. Ἐν τῇ κατὰ Ἰωάννην Ἀπάντησει, ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει 'ἐγὼ ἄγω ὑμᾶς πρὸς τὴν Ἀνατολίην' (Ἰωάν. 14,3)

in_latin.name: Anatolien
in_latin.long_meaning: Nominis Anatolien originem trahit a vocabulo Graeco Anatolίя, Oriens, dies, sicut in Oriente. Iesus in Ioanne Apostolo post Bartholomaeum dicit: 'Ego adducam vos ad Orientem' (Ioannes 14,3)

in_english.name: Anatolien
in_english.meaning: Eastern, daybreak, rising light, from the East
in_english.long_meaning: The name Anatolien originates from the Greek word Anatolίя, meaning Eastern, daybreak, rising light, from the East. In the Gospel of John, Jesus says: 'I will bring you to the East' (John 14,3). This name has strong biblical roots and signifies the rising light of God, symbolizing new beginnings and hope.

data.cultural_impact: The name Anatolien holds cultural significance as it is named after the historical region of Anatolia, which is located in modern-day Turkey. Anatolia is known for its rich history, diverse culture, and beautiful landscapes. Naming a child Anatolien would celebrate this heritage and connection to the land and its people.
data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual sense, the name Anatolien could symbolize a deep connection to the land and the divine. Anatolia was believed to be the home of the goddess Cybele, who was the goddess of nature, fertility, and mountains, among other things. Naming a child Anatolien could signify a deep appreciation for the natural world and a belief in the divine presence within it. Additionally, the name could represent a sense of rootedness and belonging to a specific place, which is an important aspect of spirituality for many people.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Anatolien is a name derived from Anatolia, the ancient region in Asia Minor. It symbolizes a deep connection to the rich spiritual heritage of early Christianity in this region, where the faith took root and spread. Anatolien embodies the strength and resilience of early Christian communities, who thrived amidst diverse cultures and challenges.

biblical_reference.note: Jesus refers to the East as a symbol of new beginnings and hope

historical_references.reference: Anatolien was a historical region in Asia Minor, named after the Anatolians, an ethno-linguistic group living in the area since at least the 3rd millennium BCE. The term Anatolian was first used by the ancient Greeks to describe the lands and peoples east of the Aegean Sea.

During the Late Roman and Early Byzantine periods, Anatolien was a major ecclesiastical province of the Byzantine Empire, centered on the city of Ancyra (modern Ankara). It was named after the ancient Anatolian city Anatolikon, meaning 'eastern' in Greek.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Christian name 'Anatolien' is of ancient origin, referring to the Anatolian Peninsula in modern-day Turkey. Today, the term is used in various modern contexts, primarily in academic, tourism, and food industries. In academia and research, Anatolian Peninsula is used to refer to the geographical area located in the western part of Asia, which has been home to numerous civilizations throughout history. In the tourism industry, Anatolian Civilizations are promoted as historical and cultural attractions, with sites like Ephesus, Troy, and Pergamum being major draws for tourists. In the food and beverage industry, Anatolian cuisine is gaining popularity, with dishes like Köfte, Börek, and Baklava being enjoyed around the world. The term is also used in culinary contexts to refer to specific ingredients like Anatolian thyme, Anatolian sumac, and Anatolian paprika, which are used in various dishes to add unique flavors and aromas.
